answer.explanation: Beacon production (scope lumen/prod) currently keeps web sessions in Redis. The approved rationale says this is because sessions must survive a web server restart. The accountable owner today is Vikram Rao.

Beacon production keeps web sessions in Redis. The stated reason is that sessions must survive a web server restart. This is an approved architecture decision for production, and Neha Iyer owns it. P08 supports that Neha is the authorized approver for Beacon/Lumen production architecture.

Beacon staging uses the Redis session store because ADR-4 requires web sessions to be stored in Redis in production and staging so sessions survive web server restarts. The approved owner as of 2026-08-01 is Vikram Rao.

Beacon staging session storage is owned by Neha Iyer under ADR-4. The approved decision says Lumen stores web sessions in Redis in production and staging and is approved and owned by Neha Iyer (P09). The governance charter also shows Neha is authorized to approve architecture for Lumen production and staging, so her ownership applies here (P08).

On 2026-07-01, the Beacon production session store decision was D4, “Redis session store.” It applied to production and was approved/owned by Neha Iyer. P09 states the decision explicitly and names Neha as the owner.

On 2026-07-01, the supported production session-store decision for Beacon is D4: Beacon stores web sessions in Redis in production and staging, approved and owned by Neha Iyer. P08 also shows Neha is the authorized approver for production architecture decisions, which matches this architecture choice.

Harbor staging users currently sign in with passkeys. The applicable decision for Harbor/staging on 2026-10-15 is D8, which replaced the earlier OIDC sign-in decision for staging only. It was approved and is owned by Priya Sharma.

Both approved decisions apply to Harbor staging as of 2026-10-15: ADR-3 says staging uses company SSO/OIDC, while the later ADR-6 says staging uses passkeys starting 2026-06-01 and replaces ADR-3 for staging only. They are equally authoritative and both environment-applicable in the retrieved passages, so the current sign-in method is in conflict.

Harbor production users sign in through company single sign-on (OIDC). The approved decision in force for production is D3, effective 2025-02-01, and its rationale says this is to provide one central access log for auditors. Ownership is Priya Sharma.

Harbor production users currently sign in through company single sign-on (OIDC). The approved architecture decision is D3, effective 2025-02-01 and applying to production; the governance charter shows Priya Sharma is authorized to approve this for production and owns the decision.

Harbor production currently uses D2, the nightly batch customer data export, because it replaced the earlier real-time export decision D1 for harbor/prod. The rationale says the real-time export saturated the production database at peak load and delayed checkout, so batching removed the peak. D2 is owned by Arjun Mehta (arjun).

Harbor production exports customer data in a nightly batch today because ADR-2 explicitly replaced the earlier real-time production behavior for production only, effective 2025-06-01. That choice was approved and owned by Arjun Mehta, who is authorized for Harbor production architecture decisions. The change was driven by INC-42, which found real-time export saturated the production database and delayed checkout; the nightly batch removes the peak. The later note from Rohan does not override this because he is not an authorized approver.

Harbor production exports customer data hourly on 2027-03-01. This is set by D9, which is effective from 2027-02-01 for production and replaces the prior nightly batch decision for that environment. The accountable owner is Arjun Mehta (arjun).

On 2027-03-01, Harbor production exports customer data hourly. The applicable approved production decision is ADR-7 (D9), which from 2027-02-01 replaces ADR-2 for production. ADR-2 had already replaced ADR-1 for production, and the governance charter shows Arjun Mehta is authorized for Harbor production architecture decisions.

Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. Decision D1 applies to harbor/staging as of 2026-10-15, and its rationale states that Harbor exports customer data in real time in production and staging because partner dashboards need fresh data. The accountable owner is Priya Sharma.

Harbor staging currently exports customer data in real time. The applicable approved decision is ADR-1 (D1), which explicitly covers staging and was approved/owned by Priya Sharma. The governance charter confirms Priya is authorized to approve architecture decisions for Harbor staging.

Beacon production follows Lumen production’s current release policy: daily releases behind feature flags, effective 2026-05-01. That decision is approved and owned by Kavya Nair. The earlier weekly-release decision was set aside for production.

Beacon production now releases daily behind feature flags, effective 2026-05-01. That decision is approved and owned by Kavya Nair. P17 shows Kavya Nair is the authorized approver for Lumen production release process changes, while Vikram Rao no longer approves them.

I could not find a supported decision answering how often Beacon staging releases at the requested date. The only applicable decision I found for Beacon staging was about Redis session storage, and the staging release-frequency decision was set aside, not currently applicable.

I couldn’t find a supported approved decision for Beacon staging release frequency. The search results returned a staging release note saying “on every merge,” but it is not shown as approved by an authorized approver for this environment, so it cannot be treated as the current governing decision.

Beacon maps to Lumen production. On 2027-01-15, the applicable decision for web sessions is D5, which says Lumen production stores web sessions in Memcached, replacing the earlier Redis decision for production only. The accountable owner is Neha Iyer.

On 2027-01-15, Beacon production keeps web sessions in Memcached. ADR-5 applies in production from 2026-12-01 and explicitly replaces ADR-4 for production only. The choice is owned by Neha Iyer, who is authorized for architecture decisions in production.

On 2027-03-01, Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. Decision D1 applies to staging and is approved by Priya Sharma; its rationale says Harbor exports customer data in real time in production and staging because partner dashboards need fresh data.

On 2027-03-01, Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The applicable approved decision is ADR-1 (D1), which explicitly covers both production and staging and says the export is real time; it is approved and owned by Priya Sharma. P01 shows Priya is authorized to approve architecture decisions for Harbor production and staging.

Beacon production follows the weekly release policy. The approved decision is D6, "Weekly releases," effective from 2025-02-15 and applicable to production on 2026-03-01. The supporting passage says Lumen production releases once a week on Tuesday, and that it is approved and owned by Vikram Rao.
On 2026-03-01, Beacon production followed D6: releases once a week on Tuesday. The decision was approved and owned by Vikram Rao.
